content:
maria (customer): Hey team — after migrating our app into the Dedicated VPC we started seeing intermittent 401s for user sessions. Seems tied to SSO redirects after login. Only affects certain requests, ~15% of traffic.

 eva (support): Sorry you're hitting this, Maria. Can you share a repro curl and the request/response headers when it fails? Any recent LB/haProxy/Ingress changes?

 maria (customer): No config changes on our side besides moving to the dedicated VPC. Repro:
 
 ```
 curl -v -L -b "REDWOOD_SESSION=<signed_cookie>" \n   -H "Host: api.customer.internal" \n   https://dedicated-vpc-edge.example.com/api/v1/chat
 ```

 On failures response is 401 from the auth service. Success responses show `x-session-verified: true` header. Failing ones have no x-session-verified and auth service logs show `missing id_token` for that trace id.

 sam (eng-runtime): Can you paste one success and one failure full header dump? Also which LB type is in front of the gateway (NLB/ALB/HAProxy/Traefik)?

 maria (customer): Fail headers (trimmed):
 ```
 GET /api/v1/chat HTTP/1.1
 Host: api.customer.internal
 Cookie: REDWOOD_SESSION=eyJhbGci...
 X-Forwarded-Proto: https
 X-Forwarded-For: 10.0.3.21
 X-Request-ID: req-7b2f9c
 ```
 Success headers include an `Authorization: Bearer <opaque-jwt>` being injected between LB -> gateway, but failing ones do not. LB is an on-prem F5 in front of a private NLB.

 derek (eng-infra): Interesting. Sounds like session-affinity/cookie handoff issue — sometimes the LB terminates TLS and rewrites cookies (signed cookie domain/path/sec flags) and then the next hop isn't sending the cookie back, so the gateway can't exchange for id_token. Do you have TCP traces or haproxy/nginx configs on the path?

 maria (customer): We captured traffic at the LB and at the gateway. On the failed flow the LB sets `Set-Cookie: REDWOOD_SESSION=...; Domain=.customer.internal; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax` but the request arriving at the gateway doesn't include the cookie.

 eva (support): That points to cookie domain/path mismatch or the LB rewriting the `Set-Cookie` then doing an internal redirect where the cookie isn't attached. Can you confirm if the failing requests are hitting a different backend shard (round-robin) vs the success ones?

 maria (customer): Yes, failures correlate with backend `pod-7` while successes go to `pod-2`. Pod-7 shows no cookie on inbound connection.

 sam (eng-runtime): Two possibilities we see in Dedicated VPC setups: 1) LB or proxy doing a follow-up internal redirect from `/` to `/api` and stripping `Cookie` header on that internal request; 2) session affinity by cookie is broken so subsequent requests land on a backend that hasn't completed the server-side session binding. Also some LBs (older F5 configs) will translate `Set-Cookie` same-site flags or chunk cookie header size causing truncation.

 derek (eng-infra): Can you run a quick tcpdump on the gateway node showing the exact HTTP bytes for a failed request? If cookie is absent at tcp level, it's upstream. If present but missing from application logs, the gateway (envoy/istio) might be configured to sanitize headers by policy.

 maria (customer): Attached tcpdump excerpt (trimmed):
 ```
 10.0.3.21 -> 10.0.4.12: GET /api/v1/chat HTTP/1.1
 Host: api.customer.internal
 Cookie:  (no cookie)
 ```
 So LB is not forwarding the cookie on those flows.

 ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0012 - "Dedicated VPC cookie loss causing SSO 401s". Pager duty page sent to eng-infra.

 eva (support): Thanks — that clarifies upstream LB behavior. Two immediate workarounds: 1) enable IP-hash session affinity on LB (so cookie not required); 2) configure LB to preserve original Set-Cookie and forward Cookie header on internal redirects (F5 iRule change). Both reduce user disruption while we root cause.

 derek (eng-infra): Long term, we should also harden the gateway to accept an alternative header for session handoff in private deployments: `x-redwood-session: <signed_cookie>` forwarded by LB. We'll add a short-term acceptor that will try `Authorization` then `x-redwood-session` before rejecting. Can you confirm whether your LB can pass custom headers?

 maria (customer): We can add custom headers, yes. If you accept `x-redwood-session` on gateway that would be easiest. Any risk of duplication or replay?

 sam (eng-runtime): We'll implement a safe acceptance flow: 1) if `Authorization` present use it; 2) else if `x-redwood-session` present validate signature server-side (same validation as cookie) and exchange for id_token; 3) strip `x-redwood-session` before proxying to internal services to avoid leakage. No new replay surface beyond current cookie model.

 eva (support): ETA for patch? Can you add a firewall rule to only allow your LB's IPs to send `x-redwood-session` header?

 derek (eng-infra): I'll whip up a canary build today and deploy to one dedicated VPC region for validation. If tests go well, we'll merge and roll to all Dedicated clusters tomorrow.

 maria (customer): Thank you — appreciate the quick turnaround. We'll configure F5 iRule to forward `x-redwood-session` for now and enable IP allowlist.

 sam (eng-runtime): For the record, config notes for ops team if you want to triage LB rules:
 ```
 # F5 iRule pseudo
 when HTTP_RESPONSE {
   if {[HTTP::header exists "Set-Cookie"]} {
     # preserve cookie header for backend internal requests
     HTTP::header replace "X-Forwarded-Set-Cookie" [HTTP::header value "Set-Cookie"]
   }
 }
 # NLB: enable proxy protocol v2 and preserve cookie header
 ```

 eva (support): Marking support ticket: SUP-5782. Will follow up when canary completes. :white_check_mark:

 maria (customer): Confirmed workaround working in canary — no more 401s on test flow. Thanks all!

 ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-0012 resolved by patch rollout to canary at 2026-03-17T14:12:00Z.
